Hand-cut layered paper art, handcrafted stop-motion paper diorama aesthetic.

Create a wide 3:2 scene (1536 x 1024), rendered entirely as handcrafted paper art, as ONE SEGMENT of a long horizontal panorama for a children's sticker puzzle. The whole image should feel like a carefully assembled paper diorama made from individually cut pieces of matte colored cardstock and fine-grain craft paper. Character stickers will be placed on it later by the program, so the scene itself contains NO characters at all.

STYLE:
Strongly emphasize the physical nature of real paper: visible paper fibers, subtle cardstock grain, crisp cut edges, slightly imperfect hand-cut contours, and tiny natural variations in shape. Use simple, graphic silhouettes and charming handcrafted forms rather than realistic modeling. Each object should be simplified into a small number of flat paper shapes, generally using only one or two solid tones per element. Avoid excessive internal detail.

Create depth primarily through PAPER LAYERING, not through realistic light-and-shadow modeling. Individual paper pieces should sit slightly above or behind neighboring layers, creating narrow, soft, clearly separated cast shadows along their cut edges, like stacked cardstock mounted with tiny spacers. Keep all shapes internally flat and evenly colored. No volumetric shading inside leaves, bean pods, soil, stones, or plants.

CRITICAL STYLE RULE:
Flat paper shapes must remain visibly FLAT.
Do not create volume by shading the interior of a shape.
A leaf, bean pod, cloud, stone, or plant must look like a flat silhouette cut from cardstock, not a miniature three-dimensional object.
Depth may appear ONLY through overlapping separate sheets and the thin cast shadow underneath their cut edges.

Use occasional very shallow debossed or embossed paper details for simple veins, folds, grooves, or decorative lines, but keep these extremely subtle. They should look pressed into paper rather than sculpted.

BANDS:
Fixed horizontal bands, identical in every segment of this board (heights as % of image height): SKY 0-40%: one flat sheet of light sky blue (#BFD8EE). FAR LAYER: a band of big flat white clouds (#F4F6FA), its top edge wandering between 32% and 46% inside the segment but EXACTLY at 40% inside both join bands. HORIZON at 46%: below it the MIDDLE GROUND, one flat sheet of paper-cream cloud floor (#F6ECD8), from 46% to 74%. GROUND LINE at 74%: below it the FRONT GROUND, one flat sheet of pale green play mat (#A8C98A), to the bottom edge. Front foreground foliage (flat toy building blocks and a few big leaves) may rise from the front ground up to 25% of the image height, but only inside the segment, never inside a join band.

JOIN BANDS (very important): the image is 1536 px wide. The LEFT 256 px (0-16.7% of the width) and the RIGHT 256 px (83.3-100%) are JOIN BANDS. Inside a join band there are ONLY the four flat colour bands described above (sky, far layer, middle ground, front ground) with their edges at exactly the fixed heights: NO objects, NO props, NO foliage, NO sun, NO clouds, NO shadows, NO light patches. The join bands let this segment be glued to the previous and the next segment of a long continuous panorama.

The LEFT join band must reproduce the attached END-BAND reference image (the last 256 px of the previous segment) exactly: same four colours, same band heights, nothing else, so that this image continues the previous segment seamlessly. The other attached full-width image is the previous segment: match its paper grain, layer spacing and shadow softness.

PLACE (only inside the middle 768 px, between the two join bands):
A round hill with a flat seven-band rainbow arch (red, orange, gold, green, sky blue, indigo, plum) and cream star cut-outs on the LEFT; a blush-pink flower bush on the RIGHT. Leave an open, flat, empty STAGE in the middle ground at the horizontal centre of the image: a plain flat patch about 36% of the image width by 37% of the image height, its bottom edge at 86% of the image height. Put the named props LEFT and RIGHT of the stage, not on it. Big shapes (a hill, a wall, a big tree) begin inside the segment and END BEFORE the join bands; nothing crosses into a join band.

PAPER PALETTE (each piece is exactly one flat colour; 10 to 20 colours in the whole image): the four band colours above plus, inside the place: sky blue #3E7CB1, bean red #A93B32, persimmon #E8703A, straw gold #D9A94E, leaf green #6E9A5B, pine green #3F6B4F, deep indigo #1F2A56, plum #7B4F8C, bark brown #6B4A32, blush pink #E9A0A0, stone grey #A9A39B.

CAMERA: far away, at eye level, straight from the front, like a tabletop diorama. No perspective, no vanishing point: every layer is a flat upright sheet seen straight on.

The attached title-screen reference of this story shows its places and props (castle, cottage, pond, tree): borrow their shapes so a child recognises the story's place, but draw NO characters from it.

FRAME:
No decorative border. The scene fills the entire frame edge to edge; the composition continues naturally beyond the top and bottom edges.

LIGHTING:
Use soft, diffuse studio-style lighting from the upper-left, mainly to reveal the edges and spacing of stacked paper layers.
Shadows should be short, soft, restrained, and consistent.
They must feel like paper-layer shadows, NOT realistic sunlight shadows cast by natural three-dimensional objects.

OVERALL FEELING:
Warm, tactile, whimsical, handcrafted, elegant, slightly imperfect, sophisticated paper craft, photographed straight from the front. All cast shadows fall toward the LOWER RIGHT (light source at the upper left), short and identical in direction on every piece.
